utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The situation as far as Judge Fluegge is concerned remains unchanged, that is, that for urgent personal reasons, he's unable to hear the case. We expect him back tomorrow. Judge Moloto and myself, we still consider it in the interest of justice to continue to hear the case and we are aware that from a distance Judge Fluegge is following the proceedings closely. Second, yesterday, I said we would start at 9.00. The reason for starting at 9.00 was that the support teams are needed in the afternoon for the Hadzic case so it was only exceptionally that we moved to a little bit earlier morning session. Since the Hadzic case will not be heard today and if I understand well, also not the coming days, this means that we can start at our usual time, 9.30. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Your next witness is Mr. Andric, I take it, Mr. Ivetic

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, Novica Andric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Andric. Before you give evidence, the rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The next is now handed out to you. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly swear that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning and greetings to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Andric. Mr. Andric, you will first be examined by Mr. Ivetic, you find Mr. Ivetic to your left standing. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: My name is Novica Andric of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to first take a look at 1D04367 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask that you take a look at the document appearing on the left-hand side of the scene and I would ask you if you remember giving this statement to the Karadzic Defence team.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could please move to the last page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again looking on the left-hand side, there is a signature and a date in 2013. Can you tell us whose signature that is?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: That is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: After signing this statement for the Karadzic trial, did you have occasion to read through the same in the Serbian language to verify if everything was correctly written?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, make some correction when you met with the Defence team members of the Mladic trial?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can now have 1D01698 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again focussing on the document that's now on the screen, do you recall giving this statement to the members of the Mladic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whose signature is visible on the first page?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: It is my signature on the front page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the last page of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, focussing on the document on the left of the screen there is a signature and a date in 2014. Could you tell us whose signature appears there?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: This is again my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, focusing on this statement given to members of the Mladic Defence team, did you read the same after signing it to ascertain if everything is correctly recorded therein?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have read it and I agree with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I were to ask you questions today about the same topics as contained in the Mladic statement, would your answers, in essence, be the same as contained in the statement?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, the answers would basically be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And sir, since you have taken a solemn declaration this morning, would those answers be truthful in nature?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we could turn to page 3 in both versions of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to look at paragraph number 7 with you. Sir, in this paragraph, you talk about needing to make a correction to what you said in the Karadzic case about not knowing the precise date when the Rogatica Brigade was placed under command and control of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With this paragraph in mind, I'd now like to return to 1D04367 and if we could look at page 4 in English, page 5 in Serbian, and paragraph 15 of the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, looking at paragraph 15 on the screen before us, does the correction that we just looked at relate to this paragraph of your Karadzic statement?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, apart from this one correction to your Karadzic statement, do you stand behind everything else as being accurate and correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Everything I said is accurate and truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if I were to ask you again today about the same topics would your answers, in essence, be the same as recorded in your Karadzic statement?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time, I would move for both 1D04367 and 1D01698 to be introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar. The number for 1D04367 would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D665, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D665 is admitted. The number for 1D01698 would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D666, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D666 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I propose to deal with the associated exhibits at the end of the testimony but I do announce that we will not be tendering any of the statements referenced in the Prosecution's response to the 92 ter motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at this time I have a short summary to read for the record of the statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed as you suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness is from Kosovo village in Rogatica municipality. His testimony is that with the formation of national parties in the early 1990s, the situation rapidly deteriorated. The SDA was first formed in 1990 with Ramiz Alabegovic spearheading the organisation. Already in late 1990 and early 1991, the first Bosnian Muslim paramilitaries were set up in Pokrivenik village and, again, Ramiz Alabegovic called the shots. After the referendum on secession of BH from Yugoslavia, nationalism grew very much and you could see that Serbs, Croats and Muslims could not live together. Bosnian Muslims were openly saying that Bosnia belonged to them and they were going to rule it. Serbs started organising village guards, using hunting rifles and legally possessed pistols. This was done especially from the second half of 1991, because volleys of automatic gunfire could be heard from Muslim villages. The witness joined the Territorial Defence on 20 April 1992 because his village was surrounded by multiple Muslim villages, and the Muslims were armed with all kinds of infantry weapons. The Rogatica Territorial Defence was armed with weapons from the Territorial Defence stocks, and was not armed by the JNA. From the first half of May 1992, there were constant provocations from Muslim villages that fired upon Serb houses with infantry weapons, anti-aircraft machine-guns, and mortars. Ramiz Alabegovic refused to heed calls to turn over weapons. Following the murders of Serbs in Ristivici village and the burning of the Serbian village of Dobromerovci, the Serbs responded to the Muslim attacks and broke their resistance. The witness denies that any mistreatment of Sefik Hurko or his father occurred whilst the same were in the garage of the witness's father. As to Rasadnik, the witness stresses that one part of the facility was a reception centre while a separate part was a detention facility. That completes the public summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have any further questions for the witness, Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to return to the statement given in the Karadzic case which has now received the number D665 and I'd like to look at the first page and paragraph 3 in both versions: In this paragraph, you talk of the formation of the SDA in 1990 in Rogatica and how Ramiz Alabegovic spearheaded the same. Could you please tell us what was this individual's position in the municipality at that time?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Ramiz Alabegovic was the police station commander in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the events surrounding the formation of the SDA in Pokrivenik village, were you present for the same or how is it that you know the information that is contained in this paragraph as to the SDA?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: The road leading towards the village of Pokrivenik passes right by my house. On that day, a large column of motor vehicles and buses was observed heading in that direction. A man called Milomir Cacic was observing the developments and he told me about it. Then in the evening both in the media and in the next day's print press, it was said that the party had been formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to turn to page 3 in both languages and focus on paragraph number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Here, sir, you talk about the wounding and subsequent death of Jela Bjelakovic can you please tell us the ethnicity of this lady and what actually happened to her?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Jela Bjelakovic is a Serb. When there were provocations from Muslims, villages Kozici and Voljevici, she was wounded and shortly thereafter she succumbed to the wounds and died.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we could turn to page 4 in the English at the bottom and page 5 in the Serbian I'd like to ask you about paragraph 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 16 of this statement, you talk about a reception -- or a holding centre in the English, a holding centre at the secondary school for all families that left Rogatica town centre after the Muslims took control. Can you please identify for us by name that secondary school?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: That was the secondary education centre was called Veljko Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to turn to Rasadnik. Sir, did you ever witness the killing of any persons that were being accommodated in Rasadnik, either in the part for detainees or in the separate part for civilians.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How often did your duties bring you to Rasadnik?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I went there rarely, mainly in order to detain the soldiers who violated military discipline by leaving their unit without permission or any other infringement of the rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were a driver within the military police. What were the instructions and orders which were received from superior officers in the military police of how to deal with enemy prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: For the most part, just like every soldier was obliged to adhere to the Geneva Conventions to provide medical assistance to the wounded, to bring them to a doctor and to have them registered by the International Committee of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for your answers to my questions on behalf of my client and the rest of my team. Thank you. That completes the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Before we continue, I have one question for you. You talked about the Veljko Vlahovic school and you said it was a collection centre. What do you understand a collection centre exactly to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, a collection centre is a place where people felt free and protected from any provocations and where simply their life was safe at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So this courtroom would be a collection centre, I would say, because people feel free, I take it, at least most of us are free. We are protected from any provocations, and our life is safe here. So this is a collection centre, do I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This was a reception or collection centre in wartime which is a place where people sought kind of safety, a house where they can put up their families in order to protect them from wartime operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's your testimony that people went freely, from their own free will, to the Vlahovic school. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: People would be safe there, protected against any evil?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How do you know that it was the situation in that school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear from anybody that there were any provocations there or at least nobody was talking about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So in the absence of any reports about a different situation, you'd call it a collection centre and you just would assume that people would go there freely. That's just your assumption or do you have any knowledge about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's my assumption. I wasn't there. I wasn't in that secondary school. I went by the school once. I saw a couple of people there who were behind the school in the courtyard playing football. They were not exposed to any combat there. I could see them move freely around the courtyard or the playground of the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd actually like to start off by asking you about some of the events surrounding Zepa in July and August of 1995. Specifically I want to ask you about your contact with a man named Avdo Palic in August of 1995. Before I do ask my questions, I should advise you that this Trial Chamber heard testimony from a witness, David Harland, that when Zepa came under sustained Serb attack after the fall of Srebrenica, ABiH Zepa commander Avdo Palic contacted the UN wanting to negotiate with the Bosnian Serbs for the evacuation of the civilians of Zepa. On the 27th of 1995, Avdo Palic voluntarily travelled in a UN vehicle under a flag of truce to a VRS position. During the negotiations when Palic wouldn't agree to surrender his military forces, members of the VRS took him away. This Trial Chamber has heard that the next day, when UN officials asked to see Palic, General Tolimir informed that Palic was dead. They've heard testimony that General Mladic told UNPROFOR that Palic was dead. I want to ask you about your contact with Avdo Palic after he was seized on the 27th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, this may be an appropriate time to review Rule 90(E) with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, as you know the Chamber, not knowing what the questions will be, follows the suggestions by the parties and therefore I'll bring Rule 90(E) to the attention of the witness. Witness, Rule 90(E) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence reads as follows. A witness, therefore that's you at this moment, a witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony. So if a truthful answer would tend to incriminate yourself, you may address me and you may object to answer that question. The Chamber will then consider that. Whatever the outcome of that is, if you're telling not the truth, you are exposing yourself to prosecution for false testimony and that is punishable by a term of imprisonment of seven years and/or a fine, a considerable fine. Therefore, if you have any concerns whether you would incriminate yourself by giving a truthful answer, don't hesitate to object. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you do know who Avdo Palic was, don't you? You need to actually speak an answer, sir, rather than just nod for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, after Palic was captured on the 27th of July, you know that he was held in an apartment in Rogatica, don't you?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you know that this is an apartment that was used by a Rogatica Brigade officer by the name of Zoran Carkic.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: During the time that Avdo Palic was being held in this apartment, you in fact brought guards to this apartment in Rogatica, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 25962 brought to our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is a 10th of August, 1995, Main Staff document signed by Colonel Beara. In the first paragraph, it refers to "Atlantida" and the first paragraph reflects that his present inadequate accommodation is attracting the interest of the public. The paragraph goes on to say that he must be transported in secret to the Mlin military prison in Bijeljina. Going on to the second paragraph, which is all I think on page 1 in the B/C/S but we may need to move to the second in English, it says that Captain Carkic would arrange with Major Kusic and personally carry out the task by announcing his arrival to Colonel Todorovic in the 1BK. Sir, isn't it true that with Captain Carkic and Major Kusic, you drove Avdo Palic to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: It is true that I drove Avdo Palic to Bijeljina with Zoran Carkic, not Major Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And sir, we see by looking at the order that driving Mr. Palic to Bijeljina was at the order of the VRS Main Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You drove Avdo Palic to Bijeljina on or about the 10th of August, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The prison where you took Palic, is that located in Bijeljina town?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it accurate that the distance between the apartment in Rogatica town and the prison in Bijeljina was about 200 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was discussed in the car on the way, what the atmosphere was like?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: In the car, we had a normal conversation. We asked him about his family because during his stay over there, conditions were put in place for him that were similar to a house atmosphere because he, indeed, was in an apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 25962.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could just see the first page of the English, I think there's a translation error. The document in English actually recorded June instead of August. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that the original says 10th, 11th of June which of course is puzzling whether in August you can order the transport of someone to take place on the 10th or the 11th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It's the Prosecution's position that the B/C/S version, the number 6 is actually an error, that the evidence and on the top of the document support this being a typographical error in the B/C/S original, Your Honours. The testimony of the witness is consistent with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In any event, I don't have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 25962 receives number P6800, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6800 is admitted. Ms. Bibles, there seems to be an implicit suggestion in your questioning that Atlantida is the same person, you have not asked the witness about it, I don't know if he's aware of the code-name used.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I apparently did not ask you this, but the code-name Atlantida which is used in this Main Staff order, you would agree that this refers to Avdo Palic?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with this code-name. I'm familiar with the name Avdo Palic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The individual that you transported on the -- approximately the 10th of August, 1995, with Captain Carkic was Avdo Palic?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you transport anybody else with Captain Carkic in this time period from Rogatica to the prison in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, Avdo Palic's body was later exhumed from a mass grave about 10 kilometres from Rogatica town. When did you last see Avdo Palic alive?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I saw Avdo Palic alive the last time in Bijeljina when I drove him to Bijeljina. I'm familiar with the journey from Rogatica to Bijeljina. I don't know anything about what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: But you're aware that his body was recovered from a grave about 10 kilometres from Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: You told me that last time when I testified in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Perhaps it was a different prosecutor who showed you that information.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to continue and go to paragraph 18 of your statement from the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, I'd like to have this clarified. You did not examine the witness in the Karadzic case, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I did not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you said it was this same Prosecutor who shared that information with you in the Karadzic case. The record will show most likely, because Ms. Bibles tells us, that she did not examine you. So how could she possibly have shared that with you in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not then, but when I testified here, somebody asked me. I don't know who it was. But in any case, that's when they told me. Somebody put that question to me at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You were asked, "Perhaps it was a different prosecutor who showed you that information." You said no. But you meant to say that it was still a Prosecutor of this Tribunal. Is that how we have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I see defence counsel have a conversation. I don't know if I should wait or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's a question about the answer at page 17, line 2 where we heard the B/C/S where he said "nije ona" which has not been inserted, which means "not her" in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to switch directions a little bit and talk about paragraph 18 of D665 which is the statement that you provided for the Karadzic case. In paragraph 18 you finish the paragraph talking about seeing on the -- I believe it's the 27th of July, Ahmet Brgulja. You describe that you spoke with this individual. You talked about cigarettes and then you say that he was transferred to Kladanj. Do you recall that section of your testimony and I believe it's in front of you.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Are you aware that he was actually detained at Rasadnik?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: He went in the direction of Kladanj with a convoy. When he was returned or when -- where he was placed, I was in Boksanica when the convoy left in the direction of Kladanj. That's when I met that man. I asked him if there were any problems. He said he didn't have any problems but that he didn't have any cigarettes. I gave him a pack of cigarettes. And the men left in the direction of Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree he was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could P3496 please be brought to our screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, what you'll see come up on the screen is a list of Muslim prisoners of war compiled by Zoran Carkic, who is the same individual you drove with in August. This list is further authorised by Tolimir and it reads: "Starting on 28 July 1995, the following citizens of Muslim ethnicity who are accommodated at the military reception centre in Rogatica ..." and I first want to ask you this is referring to Rasadnik, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Under items 1, 2 and 3, you see the names of Muslim leaders from Zepa, don't you?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I can see the names of some people but I don't know whether they were in leading positions in Zepa. I wouldn't be able to tell you that. In any case, I can see that these are Muslim names.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's look at the first name, Mehmed Hajric describes that he is the former president of the Zepa War Presidency and Muslim cleric. You would agree that he would make him a community leader or leader in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Judging by what I am reading here, I would say that that is the case. But I really don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could turn the English -- or turn to the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And for you, sir, I'd ask you to look down in the B/C/S version to number 17. Is this the individual that you saw and you believed went to Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the person's name, the first name and the family name. I don't know whether that is the person or not, judging by the name, I would say that it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And now if we could turn to the next page in B/C/S and stay on this page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I want to you look down at number 45. This is an individual that we've already discussed, Atlantida who is reflected as being in a different safe location. And again, sir, we believe that this is Avdo Palic, based on your previous testimony; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with this name, Atlantida, I don't know whether that is a reference to that person or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You know that Mr. Palic was being held in an apartment in Rogatica rather than at Rasadnik; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now if we could go to the next page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, at the top, you see a designation that talks about the health status of prisoners of war. Looking down just past halfway through the page, we see that with respect to the individual, Atlantida, he's described as "bursting" with health. Given the way that this is written, do you know what this means?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know. All I see is the English version. There is no translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you don't have a B/C/S version in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be checked whether the witness has the B/C/S version before him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, on the B/C/S page in front of you which does have some colouration, do you see about two thirds of the way down there's a section that's called "C. Treatment of prisoners of war." The line that I'm asking you to look at is just above that one. What does "puca" mean to you?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: "Puca" is part of a phrase that means fit as a fiddle. Puca is a verb that can also be used to describe shooting from a weapon but in this case, this describes his good health.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, the first three persons that we saw on this list, are you aware that they were never seen again alive?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Have you heard whether the first three individuals, the names that we looked at first on this list were located in a mass grave with the body of Avdo Palic?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber told me that during the previous trial. However, I did not know those people personally. I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm next going to shift to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I instruct you, Witness, not to again and again look at the Defence side for whatever purposes. Ms. Bibles is examining you. Just focus on what she asks you and refrain from any eye contact with others in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, next to your family home is a garage in which Sefik Hurko, Fejzo Hurko, Izeta Hurko and Abdulah Hurko were held on or about the 14th of August, 1992. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: It is true that Sefik, Fejzo, and Fejzo's wife were held there, but Abdulah wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it true that among the soldiers that you saw in your father's garage with the Hurkos was Ratko Kusic and Stojan Perkovic?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Not Ratko Kusic but Rajko Kusic and Stojan Perkovic is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: After the Hurkos were in your father's garage they were taken to Rasadnik where they were held in military detention; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: They were taken to the secondary school when they were taken away. When that collection centre was dismantled at the beginning of the school year when the purpose of the school was reinstated, those who had been in the collection centre were transferred to a new collection centre in Rasadnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask if we could have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just ask you. The question was whether they were held in military detention. You started saying they were taken to the secondary school and then later on, you again referred to them being taken to another collection centre. I think we earlier established that you have no knowledge whatsoever to allow you to conclude that this was a collection centre rather than anything else. That is valid for the school. Now, the new centre where they were taken, which one was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the Rasadnik centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 31323 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: While this document is coming up, I'll ask if you're aware that Stojan Perkovic pled guilty before a court in Bosnia to crimes committed in Rogatica including those committed in your garage, in your father's garage.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No crimes were ever committed in my father's garage. As to Stojan Perkovic having stated that, and under what circumstances, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, let's look at some of the circumstances. This document on the screen in front of you is the judgement against Stojan Perkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 in both versions and look down at number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We see that the judgement finds that he's guilty of acting together with Rajko Kusic and other members of the VRS in taking part in the illegal detention of civilians Fejzo Hurko, Sefik Hurko, Abdulah Hurko, and Izo Hurko in the garage owned by Mico Andric where he subsequently together with others committed various things and I won't go through those in detail but they are assaultive behaviours. Turning to the next page now, in the English only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said together with others. I see only one name mentioned there. Together with someone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Together with someone else. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Turning just -- let's see we're on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: "Abdulah Hurko was taken out of the garage and disappeared without a trace." Sir, the Trial Chamber has heard evidence consistent with this and I submit that your testimony today is not truthful as to what happened in your father's garage.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: These three people were taken to my father's garage, Fejzo, Sefik and Fejzo's wife. As for the fourth person, whether he was killed on the front line, I don't know. So the fourth person wasn't there. In addition, they were not locked up because the garage was being held open all the time because it was summertime. They were even served coffee when a captain came there. So this confession or this testimony given to this effect, I don't know how it came about. I claim here with full responsibility that they were not maltreated.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that I'm past the time for a break. This might be a good time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it that you'll remain within your time limits as estimated by yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take a break. Witness, I have to -- you say this is all false statements by others. Apparently those who gave those statements accepted to be punished for the events where you would not lightheartedly admit these events and your role in that if you will be punished for it, especially if you have to spend a lengthy time in prison. I do understand that the penalty imposed was 12 years of imprisonment. So therefore, I have to remind you again that if you would not speak the truth, that you are exposing yourself to prosecution and this may have severe consequences as well. I see -- I see you again as you did before smiling. It seems that it has a certain level of amusement for you. I leave it to that. We'll take the break. You may follow the usher and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. Mr. Mladic, no speaking allowed. No, just no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the witness comes in I do have two matters to bring to your attention. The first is in relation to document 31323 and perhaps Your Honours had not had time to review the same but Your Honours' characterisation of the document to the witness implied that the penalty of 12 years' imprisonment and the admissions of Mr. Perkovic related only to the event in the garage when, in fact, the judgement has multiple murders and multiple sexual assaults and rapes that are incorporated into the guilty finding. That's the first matter I wanted to raise about the characterization as presented to the witness does not comport to the document. Number 2, as I confirmed with several of my staff including counsel during the break, the witness has had the same visage, the same smiling appearance the entirety of these proceedings this morning, and indeed, that is the way he has been with us when talking throughout the week and I wanted to have that placed on the record as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have another matter: D665 which was admitted this morning should have been admitted under seal and is hereby put under seal. That's the statement -- I'll not further explain at this moment but that is the appropriate way of dealing with it. Indeed I saw that the judgement was about a 12-year imprisonment, Mr. Ivetic. Indeed, if I missed that it was for other -- for other charges as well, then it's -- I'll correct that. Witness, when I said 12 years for those who had pleaded guilty for the events in the garage, that I do understand that the sentence imposed did not deal only with that fact but also with other facts. That's hereby corrected. Further, Mr. Ivetic informed me that you may have a kind of a natural smile which should not be misinterpreted. We'll take that into consideration. That doesn't change that you're addressing now and then and seeking eye contact with the Defence part of this courtroom and you are advised not to do that. Ms. Bibles, if there's any -- if you have any further questions, you still have an hour to go so therefore you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I would first tender 65 ter 31323 at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection. I think there's another prior document to that had not been admitted, the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I believe that's now P6800.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the present one just tendered, Madam Registrar, would receive ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31323 receives P6801.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6801 is admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, switching topics a little bit and referring more to paragraph 7 of this statement that you prepared for the Mladic Defence. I'd like to talk a little bit about the Rogatica Brigade. First, you've told us that you were, I believe, a driver policeman in the military police of the Rogatica Brigade. Was the commander of the Rogatica Brigade Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 31390 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, coming up on the screen, we'll see a document signed by General Sipcic on 14 June 1992. It appears that's now on our screens. We see in number 2, he's directing various supplies be provided as requested by the Rogatica Brigade. So here, sir, you would agree that by the 14th of June, 1992, the command of the VRS through the SRK was sending supplies to the Rogatica Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of that because by October 1992, I had been in the village. This happened much earlier, therefore, I cannot confirm it because it was only in October that I joined the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's take a look at another document and see if that assists in understanding this process for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could look at 65 ter 8922.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document from Commander Kusic to the command of the SRK, dated 15 July 1992. Do you recognise Commander Kusic's signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I can see that there's a signature underneath the name. Whether this is Rajko Kusic's signature or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Bibles, you called this document as dated 15th July, I see it's 15th June.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, I was wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It is a 15 June 1992 document, sir. I apologise for the mistake in the date. Sir, if you could look at the third paragraph, we see a description of the brigade's officers, junior officers and soldiers, et cetera. Is that consistent with your recollection of the Rogatica Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I am telling you again that I came to the brigade command only in October. Whether this was the strength at the time, it may have been so but then again, it might not. I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, at the very top of the document, I direct your attention to the first paragraph where the commander describes that: "Large numbers of Muslims, mostly women and children, are arriving in the town every day. The people are being moved into the premises of the secondary school centre." Is this the school that you have been talking about?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you see at the top as well that this is described as a regular report to the command of the SRK.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know when the Rogatica Brigade was placed under the command and at what time it started sending armed reports. I was a regular soldier, therefore I was not familiar with the procedure of when and for how long these reports were being sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Based on what you see on the screen here, would you agree that by -- certainly by the 15th of June, 1992, that these sort of regular reports were being issued?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, for this particular date, that is true. But whether it happened on a daily basis, I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender 65 ter 8922 and 31390.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We would object. I don't think the witness has been able to add anything to the document or attest to any kind of authenticity issues for the document. He stated that he doesn't know so that cannot be a basis for admitting these documents through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objection against them being bar-tabled being connected to the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I believe, according to your Chamber guidance, all the bar table motions for the Prosecution should have been filed already. It is improper for the Prosecution to present positive evidence not -- not recognised by a witness during the Defence case in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I would tender it from the bar table, Your Honour. It was raised by the paragraph 7 in the witness's statement with respect to his lack of knowledge about the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further response to that, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again it's not able to be confirmed by the witness, therefore in that sense it's a document that's being presented apart from this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's what Ms. Bibles, I think, expressed by saying that she now sought it be admitted from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. It's common practice in this courtroom that documents directly related to the content of the witness may be tendered from the bar table even if the witness is unable to identify the document or -- Madam Registrar, the numbers would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31390 receives number P6802 and document 8922 receives number P6803, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6802 and P6803 are admitted. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified that in October of 1992, you were recalled to Rogatica to the brigade command. I'd like to ask you first if you recall at that time that you reported to the SRK?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Do I recall what?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you recall that through the brigade command, Rogatica Brigade then went up through the SRK as it went up through the structure of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I was called to come to the command of the brigade to work as a driver for the military police, and that was in October.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll move on. Sir, in paragraph 17 of your -- I'll refer to as the Karadzic statement so that you know which one we're talking about -- you tell us that you were in Rasadnik often enough to know about the meals eaten by the detainees as well as work done by the detainees. Do you also know the warden was Vinko Bosic also known as Vili?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could now have 65 ter 31330 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, as this comes up on the screen, you'll see that it's a 1 February 1993 list of prisoners of war in the Vili camp in Rogatica. As you look at the top of the document, would you agree that this document is referring to what was more commonly known as Rasadnik?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: This refers to the Rasadnik facility and not the Vili facility. The Vili facility did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So by the reference of "Vili", is this referring to prisoners of war as the document stays, that are being held at Rasadnik; is that correct? Have we cleared up that confusion?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: So there was Rasadnik, not Vili. It did not exist at all. There was a military remand detention and the Rasadnik collection centre that had been moved from the secondary school so these are two separate facilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, sir, you see at the very top of the page, this is a document the Drina Corps Command dated 1 February 1993. On the top it reads: "Pursuant to your request, we are forwarding the list of prisoners of war in the Vili camp, Rogatica." So there's no confusion. These prisoners of war we're referring to are being held in the Rasadnik facility; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: These are the men that were held at the reception centre although I haven't read the whole list, I don't see that anyone was in the military detention so there was a military detention on one side, and the reception centre on the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, sir, again you appear to be trying to interpret this list in a way that you understand you should be interpreting it. Instead I would rather ask you to just read what this document actually portrays. You would agree the top of the list talks about a list of prisoners of war; correct? That's what it reads on top; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: That's what's written at the top but women were never prisoners of war, at least not in our practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, sir, let's go through the list then. You seem to be anticipating what I was going to ask and that is, as you look down the list, many of the names that you see, the first names are female Muslim names; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That would be Biba or Nura, those are women's names; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And at number 4, we see a woman whose first name -- would you agree that number 4 refers to a woman?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that her date of birth being 1892 meant that she was 101 years old in 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender 31330.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31330 receives number P6804, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could now have 65 ter 31329 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this as it comes up is a different document. It's a list -- I'll wait until it comes up. As this list comes up on your screen, you see that it is a list of "captured persons of Muslim ethnicity," and it is dated 10 April 1993. This list was sent by the Drina Corps Command Lieutenant-Colonel who received the last list that was before you. He's now sending this larger list to the command of the East Bosnia Corps and to the Ministry of Justice and Administration. Now, sir, as you look under Rogatica, you see the same women on this list that were on the previous list. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And now if we could go down in both versions so we can see number 32. I believe we may have to turn to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If you look at number 32, do you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: This is a male name but I don't know the person myself. But I can deduce that it's a man's name.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that in the summer of 1993, you drove a bus from Rasadnik to Zvornik with the Rasadnik warden and with Zoran Carkic filled with prisoners from Rasadnik including this man, number 32, a pregnant woman, and other individuals who were obviously civilians.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: It is not true that I drove a bus. I escorted the bus in a police car as far as Zvornik. These civilians were supposed to be let go through to the territory controlled by the ethnic community that they belonged to. All I did was escort the bus to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you would agree that prior to the date that you escorted the bus on which they were transported, these were civilians who had been detained in Rasadnik; correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: These were civilians who were at the reception centre and they were on the list in order to be exchanged along with the others because all of them were supposed to be exchanged. So there was a military detention and a reception centre. These were two different facilities, one next to the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, sir, in your testimony, you've described that you didn't spend a lot of time at Rasadnik. You've been presented with a list of prisoners of war who include clearly civilians, and yet you keep saying that there was a separation at Rasadnik. Isn't it true, sir, that you don't know -- you don't have personal knowledge that the civilians were handled differently and, in fact, the evidence that you've been presented would support that these civilians were considered prisoners of war and were actually being held in the Rasadnik centre as such.

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: When I came to Rasadnik, I saw the civilians there in another pavilion adjacent to the one. They were freely moving in front of the pavilion in the courtyard which means that they were not locked up as opposed to the soldiers who were held in detention.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree that these civilians were not free to go and, in fact, to leave, they were placed on a bus and transported under military police escort?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: They requested to cross over to the territory. They couldn't do it independently. They wanted to go to the territory under the control of their own people. It was impossible for them to cross the separation line independently without any prior agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, the reason for that is what we've seen and the way they're characterised in these documents and that is captured persons of Muslim ethnicity and prisoners of war. Isn't that accurate? That's the way they came to Rasadnik; isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I have to go back to what I said that Rasadnik was a new collection centre. There was a pavilion where they were housed and there was a military detention where the soldiers were kept. However when the academic year started they had to be moved. Therefore, they were free to move around, but they couldn't cross over to a different territory without any agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you have described several times now that they were free to move on the yard of where they were kept. Does that mean that they were also free to leave those premises and go home or go to their family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some of the people from the list, specifically from the Burati village and because of the safety situation in the village, they wanted to go to the territory controlled by the army of their own people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question, where you emphasise several times that you saw them moving on the courtyard. My question was where were they free to leave that courtyard and go to wherever they wished to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they could go but they couldn't cross over to the territory that they desired to go to. They wouldn't do that on their own. It had to be organised and based on an agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they could have left the courtyard and could have gone home without any problem; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, not all of them probably didn't have houses that were intact. Some of them were damaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that's not my question. My question is whether they wanted to go to their family, to whatever place, irrespective of whether their own houses were destroyed, to go home, to go to wherever they wished to go, is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were free to go but they felt safer there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then that, perception seems to be not very consistent with the words used, that is, "captured" "prisoners of war" are these concepts or these documents all false or what -- do you have an explanation why those who prepared these documents describe them not as civilians free to go wherever they want but as civilians captured and prisoners of war? Do you have any explanation for that use of language by those who drafted these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know why these terms were used in the way they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You further told us that they were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say that they were exchanged. I said they had gone to be exchanged and the agreement concerning the exchange was for them to go to Tuzla from Zvornik. However, the Muslim authorities undermined this agreement and did not allow them to cross over and some of these people were sent back to Rogatica a day or two later because they were banned from entering their territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, but at least you said they were on the list to be exchanged. Why was there an exchange if -- you could just have released them? Why would you need others to receive and return if these people were free to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. That's how things were in that case. I don't know what happened. It was beyond me to make any decisions or see to what was going on. My only task was to provide escort all the way to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand and I didn't ask you about personal responsibility for that, but where you emphasise so much that they were free to go, at the same time you say, I do not understand why but they were there and supposed to be exchanged. Exchange being a concept which is not very consistent with free choice to go wherever you want.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw them there and they were moving around freely in front of the pavilion where they were accommodated. That is where I saw things. It was my estimate. Nobody kept them enclosed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You also told us that they were supposed to be exchanged and for that reason on the list, lists which describe them as being captured and being prisoners of war. We've heard your explanation, Ms. Bibles will now put her next question to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I couldn't find it in the transcript. Did you briefly testify that the two Hurkos, the father and son who were in your father's garage were later taken into military detention?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in Rogatica, they were in the military prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, if you could look at the list in front of you and look at the names under 31 and 33 on this list, aren't they the same individuals?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, by name.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And on the same list is the woman who was 101 years old; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, the reference you were apparently looking for is -- let me have a look. I had it a second ago. Indeed the transcript reflects that the witness said that they were taken in military detention. It's somewhere on page 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I would tender this document, 65 ter 31329.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31329 receives number P6805, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And finally, sir, I'd ask if we could have 31336 on our screens. And I'd ask that we go to page 9 in the English and page 7 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, is this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, it was 21, line 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm afraid it was your question whether they were held in military detention. You asked whether that was correct. And the witness said they were taken away. So not directly confirming that they were taken in military detention. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, on the screen in front of you is a portion of an exhumation report on a mass grave. And this one as we see on the page refers to bodies exhumed from Rasadnik in Rogatica. There were 14 bodies recovered here or exhumed here. The first one that we see here is Hanka Kustura born in 1895.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if we turn the page, looking for number 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We see a woman who was born in 1898. Following her, is a body of a man who was born in 1928. Sir, isn't it true that a number of civilians died in captivity at Rasadnik?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. They may have died, but I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Bibles. One second, please. Yes, Judge Moloto has a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, for Ms. Bibles. Ms. Bibles, what do you want to do with 31336?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's been no foundation been laid for its admission in this format.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. I'm just looking at the document. If you give me just a few seconds to ... Ms. Bibles, your question was whether people died when in Rasadnik. We see that these are relatively old people. Is there any autopsy report available for those witnesses? I mean there was a bit of a suggestion that they may have died not of natural causes and that people at that age, I think we have to be very careful to make any such suggestion. Now, I had insufficient time to look at it more clearly and I'm not entirely familiar with the document. Could you tell us a bit more about the document which may be relevant for the decision of admission as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is a court document from Bosnia. Actually what I was thinking in the interest of time is perhaps we could MFI this document. I would like to investigate the autopsies behind these. I have to admit, I do not have that information at my fingertips and then we could raise this at a later time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Also because it's a mass grave and at the same time I see grave dimensions described here which are not the same which of course for a mass grave is somewhat surprising. I see two metres by 90 centimetres, two and a half metres by one metre and -- it's all relatively unclear to me at this very moment. The document will be marked for identification. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31336 receives number P6806, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and I was wondering if counsel could direct to us where it actually says mass grave. I have yet to find except for one number 22 that it is a collective grave. All the others appear to be individual grave sites, not mass graves as was presented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That may be part, then, of the further clarifications Ms. Bibles will provide us with. And she certainly will also pay attention to what you just observed, Mr. Ivetic. Any further questions, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to return to the questioning of yourself in relation to Mr. Avdo Palic on behalf of Ms. Bibles earlier today. Were you ever interviewed by the Bosnian authorities in relation to the disappearance of Avdo Palic?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was interviewed at the administration of the crime prevention police in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When, approximately, did that interview take place?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember. It may have been in 2005 or 2008. I really can't remember when exactly -- it was after the events, around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what kind of interview was it? Could you describe the interview?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: I was asked whether I knew what happened to Avdo Palic after Bijeljina. I didn't. I was put on a polygraph and it was established by way of using the lie detector that I really didn't know what happened to him after Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Have you been interviewed by the Bosnian authorities relating to Avdo Palic since that one interview where a polygraph was administered and it was established you didn't know what happened to him after Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to return with you to the conversation in the automobile while you and Mr. Carkic were driving with Mr. Palic towards Bijeljina. How would you describe the level of familiarity between Mr. Palic on the one hand and Mr. Carkic on the other?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: They had known each other from before because Avdo Palic had worked in the water cleaning facility so their conversation was rather normal during the entire journey to Bijeljina. Avdo Palic was sitting in the car just like we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How would you describe the mood of those in the automobile?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Both Palic and Carkic spoke in a very normal way without any tensions as two people who knew each other. As simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can go back in time towards the time period when Mr. Palic was at the apartment in Rogatica. Could you perhaps first tell us something about the conditions of the apartment, the living conditions?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: The living conditions were equal to living in one's own house. Avdo Palic could use the bathroom. Carkic at one point brought him a change of clothes so he could change into them. It was a proper home atmosphere.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, during the Prosecution's examination, it was brought up that you had transported some guards to that apartment. Did you ever have an occasion to view the interactions between Mr. Avdo Palic and those guards?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Avdo Palic and the guards, when I arrived there, played cards. On one occasion when I arrived, they were playing cards. Again, it was a home atmosphere. He was surrounded by a proper home atmosphere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to make everything clear, he was detained there, wasn't he? He was imprisoned in that apartment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was accommodated there together with -- he could not leave on his own. He was actually moved away so nothing bad would happen to him because apparently Avdo Palic had been in command of an action in Bokcin Potok where 75 people had been killed so he was sheltered from anybody who made -- may have done something bad to him in retaliation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But he was on a list of prisoners of war, wasn't he? I mean if you are in detention, that may provide some safety from attacks from others but it doesn't change the fact that you are in detention.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was on a list of prisoners of war and we saw him on that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you proceed, Mr. Ivetic. Witness, at page 43, line 8, Mr. Ivetic asked you: "During the Prosecution's examination it was brought up that you had transported some guards to that apartment." Your answer said "When I arrived there, he was playing cards." It looks like you are at cross purposes with Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic is asking about the guards that you transported there not the guards that you found playing cards. Can you make sure that you are on the save wavelength with Mr. Ivetic. You may proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you answer the Judge's question? Which guards are you talking about? Are you talking about the same guards, the different guards, which guards were playing cards with Mr. Palic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are interested in the guards that drove there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour I'm trying to find out the witness's answer to find out which guards he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us which guards you were talking about that were playing cards with Mr. Palic?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Obrenovic, Goran Ristanovic and Zdravko or Danko Frganja I can't remember the first name. When I visited them, and when I brought them food, not immediately when I transported them there, when I visited them, when you asked me about the atmosphere that prevailed there, I answered that on one occasion, on one of my visits, I found the guards playing cards with Avdo Palic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to be clear, sir, are these the same guards that you had previously transported to the apartment?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were the same people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just try to make matters clear. You brought guards there, I take it, but please correct me when I'm wrong, to ensure that Mr. Palic would not leave the apartment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I drove those people there because they were to be accommodated there with Avdo Palic who would protect him, who would protect him from anybody's knee-jerk reaction in retaliation for some past events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, that's a different concept of being imprisoned. You say he wasn't imprisoned, he was there just to be protected against outsiders. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, both protected and kept indoors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the guards were there to keep him indoors which would at the same time protect him against any outsiders coming in; is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move to another topic, your father's garage and the allegations of Mr. Stojan Perkovic as to the treatment of the Hurko family in the garage. How would you describe the interactions with the Hurkos in the garage?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: When the Hurko family members arrived in the garage, they were not incarcerated there. They were given coffee. Those people -- we knew them, they lived not far away from us. They spent only about 15 minutes there and then Captain Cerovic arrived. They were not ill treated at all. I claim that with full responsibility. As for Perkovic's statement, I don't know under what conditions it was given but I claim with full responsibility that those people were not ill treated at all while they were in the garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were either of the Hurkos asked where they had gotten the gun or the ammunition for the gun, the bullets?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Fejzo and Sefik Hurko were asked where the ammunition had come from and he said that he got them from the Leleks. They were their neighbours and both pistols and ammunition were found on that premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move to the bus full of persons that you escorted to Zvornik. Did anyone use force or threats against those being transported in the bus?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: No. They got on the bus and in Zvornik they were accommodated in a centre. I don't know its name. And the following morning, they were either let go or exchanged or I don't know what. In any case, nobody forced them to get on the bus. Nobody ill treated them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What precisely were your orders in relation to escorting the bus?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: My order was to escort the bus from Rogatica to Zvornik and to hand over people to somebody. Captain Carkic did that. They were accommodated and then early in the morning, the next day, they were -- I don't know, exchanged or released or something. I don't know what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you said earlier today that some of these people had been banned from entering their territory. Who banned them?

utterances.speaker: NOVICA ANDRIC
utterances.text: Muslim authorities obstructed the agreement on letting them go to the territory in the direction of Tuzla. I don't know why. It was their authorities who did not allow them to enter their own territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you clarify the use of the language "their territory." I mean had they lived in that area before? Witness, had they lived at the other side of the line or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't live on the other side of the line. They requested to be allowed to go to the territory controlled by the army of their own people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say, therefore, if you refer to "their territory," you do not mean the territory where they had lived before but you mean the territory controlled by the Muslim authorities. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my question intended "their territory" being the "their" of the people who banned them. That was how my question was phrased, that someone had banned them from coming to "their territory".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
